correctness.rationale: For all integer n>=1 and reciprocal passive layers with 0<r,t, r+t<=1, f_i maps [0,1] strictly increasingly into [0,1]. Exact 2x2 matrix commutator yields sign[f_i(f_j(x))-f_j(f_i(x))]=sign(w_j-w_i) strictly for unequal w at all x including 1. Strictly increasing prefixes propagate swaps; bubble sorting proves all optimal orders and ties. Algebraic K-M solution has w=2(1+K/S), independent of thickness including K=0. The packaged standard-library checker independently passed 4,800 exact commutator/sign cases, 10,944 exact permutation comparisons and rational exemplar identities. No numerical finiteness is used to prove general n.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the complete n-layer global top-reflectance maximization/minimization and equality characterization for all backing albedos and positive layer thicknesses. Kubelka 1954 already supplies the adding formula and exactly the same intrinsic w=2a index for three-sheet transmittance; neither is newly claimed. Its experimental permutation statement concerns transmissivity and darkest-middle placement, not the universal top-reflectance optimum. Hébert et al. 2007 give a substantially broader composition framework but the inspected relevant portions and full-text search did not locate or imply a universal sorting formula without the additional adjacent-swap analysis. Direct mathematical record queries produced only unrelated ranked matches, not a corresponding result. Literature priority remains provisional, especially broader operator theorems and an abstract-only 2015 survey.
residual_risks: The complete 2015 two-flux survey was not materially read; an equivalent known rearrangement theorem might be present.
Other monographs on industrial paint optical stacking and atmospheric albedo could contain the identical global sorting criterion or an immediate stronger generalization.
The theorem is an ideal monochromatic symmetric diffuse model and has no claim for real spectral or angular atmospheres.

value.rationale: Layer rearrangement is a natural finite experimental-design and atmospheric-albedo optimization problem. An n! search collapses to a single physically interpretable rule, simultaneously valid for all backing albedos and arbitrarily unequal thicknesses; complete equality and min/max classification rules out tie ambiguity. The intrinsic ratio differs from individual-sheet measured reflectance and can change the actual optimum (illustrated by B-A-C versus raw-reflectance B-C-A). This is nontrivial physical structure even though it has a short proof from classical adding laws.
